title: Owner Settings: make Support access reachable (a chip row instead of a Segments control that only renders three options), and let the owner approve for the hours asked or fewer, or refuse, on desk and phone
rootCause:
The fix is frontend only; owner-service is correct and tested. Every citation was re-read on b59bbf0.

1. WHY THE VIEW NEVER RENDERS. frontend/owner-app/app/settings/index.tsx:248-260 passes FOUR items to `<Segments testID="settings-view">` (business, numbering, flags, support). The kit draws only the first three in both renderers, `items.slice(0, 3)` at frontend/libs/ui/src/web/controls.tsx:387 and frontend/libs/ui/src/native/controls.tsx:421, by design (frontend/libs/ui/src/types.ts:342 "Two or three options"; docs/design/UX-00-design-system.md:426). So 'support' is dropped silently, and the view at index.tsx:433-444 with its query at :62-64 (`enabled: view === 'support'`) cannot be reached on any platform or width. QA/evidence/phase1/admin/ow-01-settings.txt and ow-03-settings-phone.txt list exactly Business profile, Numbering series, Feature flags. A fifth level-2 route tab would not work either: the /settings PAGE_TABS group already holds four (Settings, Imports, Messages, Audit) and `<Tabs>` slices to four (web controls.tsx:246, native controls.tsx:315). The established repair is a single-select `<Chips>`: frontend/manager-app/app/inbound/index.tsx:280-299 and frontend/manager-app/app/billing/credit-notes.tsx:414-429. frontend/admin-app/app/support.tsx:66-69 documents the same limit.

2. EVEN WITH THE VIEW VISIBLE, THE OWNER COULD NOT DECIDE AS THE FINDING EXPECTS.
 a. index.tsx:84 always sends `hours: 4`. owner-service refuses hours above requestedHours with 400 window_too_long (backend/libs/core/src/modules/tenancy/support.service.ts:116-121). It counts the window from the REQUEST (:124-127) and refuses a window that has already closed with 409 request_expired (:128-132). So every ask under 4 h fails, and a 72 h ask is cut to 4 h counted from the ask.
 b. There is no Refuse. The action column (index.tsx:212-239) offers Approve on `requested` and Revoke on `active`, nothing else. The contract's refusal is `revoke` on a requested row, which the server records as `rejected` (support.service.ts:168-203, statusOf :276-280; backend/libs/contracts/src/tenancy.ts:445-450).
 c. A phone has no decision buttons. Approve and Revoke live in a Register column with no `priority`. The phone rendering draws only the identity, value and chip columns as ListRows (frontend/libs/ui/src/web/list.tsx:513-540, frontend/libs/ui/src/native/list.tsx:380-400), and this register has no `onSelect`. So 390 px web, Android and iOS give no way to decide.
 d. The confirm dialog (index.tsx:451-457) prints only "Support window": no reason, requester, scope or hours. `.then(done, done)` (:466-467) closes it on failure, so a 400 or 409 looks as if nothing happened. This is the DOS-029 pattern, repaired so far only in the manager app (frontend/manager-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:194-234).
 e. On desk, the history register heads the reason column t('o3.note') = "Note for the person who asked" (index.tsx:199). That label misnames the requester's reason, which is the text the owner is meant to read.

3. WHAT THE CLIENT HAS TO WORK OUT ITSELF. `toGrant` sends `expiresAt: null` for a requested row (support.service.ts:298), and there is no lapsed status yet (DOS-110). An ask whose own hours have run out therefore still reads `requested`. The console already handles this with `askLapsed()` (frontend/admin-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:365-372: requestedAt + requestedHours x 3 600 000 <= now). The owner app must use the same rule, or it offers an Approve that can only answer 409.

4. THE BACKEND IS NOT AT FAULT.
 - Contract: tenancy.ts:462-492. Permissions: permissions.ts:392-394, all OWNER_ONLY.
 - Rules are covered by backend/libs/core/src/modules/tenancy/support.spec.ts:119-279.
 - The finding's api-42 approve returned 200.
 - dos_qa (SELECT only) matches the finding. Tarsun: 7232298a (dos.support, 4 h, asked 12:50 IST 12 Sep, never answered, now lapsed), dc9b8792 (dos.admin = 'Rohit Nair (Distribution OS)', 72 h, approved then revoked) and a6b5683f (expired). Sai: 01a095f1 (approved 2 h, revoked).
 - Nothing notifies the owner of an ask: the only 'support.requested' is a platform_audit action (backend/libs/core/src/modules/platform-admin/support.service.ts:88).

5. THE SAME SILENT SLICE ELSEWHERE IN THE OWNER APP (NOT PART OF THIS FINDING). Four more surfaces pass four items to `<Segments>`, and each fourth view can only be reached through that control:
 - frontend/owner-app/app/prices/index.tsx:233-246 ('quote', rendered at :312)
 - staff/index.tsx:134-146 ('bounds', :194)
 - stock/catalog.tsx:143-156 ('brands', :236)
 - src/lib/ui.tsx:219-242 RangeSegments ('This FY'), used on billing/index, billing/credit-notes, money/index, money/books and money/receipts.
No finding covers them (grep of QA/findings for RangeSegments, This FY and slice(0, 3)). They are raised under decisionsNeeded; this fix does not touch them.

changes.what:
Pure rules: no React, no @dos/ui. Imports only `type SupportGrant` from @dos/contracts.
- `type SettingsView = 'business' | 'numbering' | 'flags' | 'support'` and `SETTINGS_VIEWS: readonly { id: SettingsView; labelKey: string }[]`: business → o24.business, numbering → o24.numbering, flags → o24.flags, support → o24.support. Same shape as VIEWS in manager-app/app/inbound/index.tsx.
- `APPROVAL_HOURS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 72] as const`. The contract allows 1-72; the console asks from 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 72 (admin-app/src/lib/support.tsx:42).
- `windowClosesAt(requestedAt: string, hours: number): string` = new Date(Date.parse(requestedAt) + hours * 3_600_000).toISOString(), measured exactly as support.service.ts:124-127 measures it.
- `askLapsed(grant, now)`: the console's rule word for word (admin-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:365-372), copied with a comment that names it. Apps cannot import each other, and DOS-110 is expected to replace both copies with a server status.
- `supportDecision(grant: Pick<SupportGrant, 'status' | 'active' | 'requestedAt' | 'requestedHours' | 'expiresAt'>, now: number)` returns:
  - `{ kind: 'open', actions: ['revoke'], closesAt: expiresAt }` when `active`;
  - `{ kind: 'waiting', actions: ['approve', 'refuse'], hours, initialHours: requestedHours }` when status is `requested` and not askLapsed. `hours` is the ascending union of APPROVAL_HOURS and requestedHours, keeping each h <= requestedHours whose windowClosesAt(requestedAt, h) is strictly after now (the server refuses <= now);
  - `{ kind: 'closed', actions: [] }` for rejected, revoked, expired and lapsed grants.
- `chosenHours(decision, picked: number | undefined): number` returns `picked` while it is still in decision.hours, otherwise initialHours. A choice whose window closed while the page stayed open is never sent.

Red-first commit: SETTINGS_VIEWS as above (it is data), and stubs that reproduce today's behaviour:
- supportDecision: requested → { kind: 'waiting', actions: ['approve'], hours: [4], initialHours: 4 }, active → revoke, anything else closed, with no lapsed check;
- windowClosesAt counts from Date.now(), the approval-time reading the server rejects;
- chosenHours returns 4.
The DOS-108 specs then fail on their assertions rather than on a missing import (the approach 31af220 took for DOS-025).

The three DOS-108 rule specs listed under tests. Fixtures are shaped like the dos_qa Tarsun grants: 7232298a (requested, 4 h, asked 12:50 IST 12 Sep), dc9b8792 (approved 72 h, then revoked) and a6b5683f (expired). Two more fixtures: the template's live 72 h window and a fresh 2 h ask. All run against a fixed `now`. The file imports only vitest and ./support.

(a) Imports.
- Replace the local `type View` (:37) with the imported SettingsView.
- Import SETTINGS_VIEWS, supportDecision, chosenHours and windowClosesAt from '../../src/lib/support'.
- Add `Chips` to the @dos/ui import (:13-28). KEEP `Segments`: settings-pod (:378-383) still uses it for the three POD policies.
- Import `Refusal` and `stayOpen` from '../../src/lib/ui'.

(b) View switch. Remove `<Segments testID="settings-view">` from `actions` (:248-260); the business Save button stays there. Render `<Chips testID="settings-view" items={SETTINGS_VIEWS.map((entry) => ({ id: entry.id, label: t(entry.labelKey), selected: view === entry.id }))} onToggle={(id) => { setView(id as SettingsView) }} />` as the first child of the Screen body. Carry over the 'four views, so a chip row' comment from manager-app/app/inbound/index.tsx:280-287.

(c) State. `grantAction` (:52) becomes 'approve' | 'refuse' | 'revoke' | null. Add `hoursById: Record<string, number>`, so one request's hour choice never carries into another (the DOS-153 lesson).

(d) Mutations.
- approveGrant (:82-86) takes `{ id: string; hours: number }` and sends `tenancy.support.approve({ id, hours, idempotencyKey: meta.idempotencyKey })`. The fixed `hours: 4` goes.
- revokeGrant (:87-91) is unchanged and serves both Refuse and Revoke. The server records rejected or revoked from approved_at, so there is no client-side status.

(e) History register (:196-240).
- Drop the 'action' column. No phone rendering can reach it, and it would be a second decision path still carrying the old fixed hours.
- Add `textColumn('closes', t('o24.closes'), (row) => instantWithClock(row.expiresAt))`.
- Head the reason column t('o24.reason') instead of t('o3.note').

(f) Support view (:433-444). Inside the existing Async, render a `<Stack gap={6}>` holding:
  - One `<Panel testID={`support-card-${row.id}`} title={row.requestedByName} meta={word(row.scope)}>` per grant whose `supportDecision(row, Date.now()).kind !== 'closed'`. Each shows Field t('o24.reason') = the reason word for word, Field t('o24.hoursAsked') = t('o24.hoursCount', { count: row.requestedHours }) and Field t('o3.asked') = instantWithClock(row.requestedAt).
  - Waiting: `const chosen = chosenHours(decision, hoursById[row.id])`, then:
    - `<Chips testID={`support-hours-${row.id}`}>` over decision.hours, labelled t('o24.hoursCount', { count: h }), selected when h === chosen; onToggle stores hoursById[row.id];
    - a secondary Txt t('o24.countedFromAsk');
    - Field t('o24.openUntil') = instantWithClock(windowClosesAt(row.requestedAt, chosen));
    - primary Button t('o24.approveFor', { count: chosen }), testID support-approve-<id>;
    - `variant="destructive"` Button t('o24.refuseSupport'), testID support-refuse-<id>.
    Each button sets grantId and grantAction.
  - Open: Field t('o24.openUntil') = instantWithClock(decision.closesAt) and a destructive Button t('o24.revokeSupport'), testID support-revoke-<id>.
  - No card at all: Txt t('o24.noneWaiting').
  - Then the existing Register (settings-support), as history.
  The cards are page-level Panels, not a Sheet, so the Dialog they open is never a second native Modal over a Sheet (DOS-164).

(g) Dialog (:446-470). It looks the grant up by grantId in grants.data.items.
  - Title: o24.approveSupport, o24.refuseSupport or o24.revokeSupport.
  - Body, a Stack:
    - the sentence: t('o24.confirmApprove', { who, scope: word(scope), until: instantWithClock(windowClosesAt(requestedAt, chosen)) }), t('o24.confirmRefuse', { who }) or t('o24.confirmRevoke', { who });
    - the reason word for word;
    - as the LAST child, `<Refusal of={[approveGrant, revokeGrant]} scope={grantId === null || grantAction === null ? null : `${grantId}:${grantAction}`} testID="settings-support-refusal" />`.
  - confirmLabel: t('o24.approveFor', { count: chosen }) for approve, the title otherwise. `destructive` for refuse and revoke. `busy` as today.
  - onConfirm: `void approveGrant.mutateAsync({ id: grantId, hours: chosen }).then(done, stayOpen)` or `void revokeGrant.mutateAsync(grantId).then(done, stayOpen)`, replacing `.then(done, done)` at :466-467.

Add `RefusalProps`, `Refusal` and `stayOpen`, copied from frontend/manager-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:194-234 together with their DOS-029 comment. They use useRefusal and type WriteOutcome from '@dos/api-client/react'. `Refusal` prints refusal.message in colors.status.brick.fg, and t('app.writeNoConnection') for a network error, because nothing queues an owner write. In this fix only the Settings dialog uses them; the owner app's other `.then(done, done)` dialogs are not touched.

New keys in the o24 block (:577-616):
- 'o24.refuseSupport': 'Refuse access'
- 'o24.approveFor': 'Approve for {count} h'

In the app block: 'app.writeNoConnection': 'No connection. Check the signal, then press again.' (copied from manager-app/src/strings.ts:47).

Placeholders use the kit's `{name}` interpolation (frontend/libs/ui/src/strings.ts:152). word.read_only and word.read_write already exist (:808-809).

Add the script "test": "vitest run --dir src" (the sales-app form) and the devDependency "vitest": "catalog:", as commit 31af220 did for @dos/manager-app. The frontend `turbo run test` then includes the owner app.

decisionsNeeded:
Neither decision blocks implementation; default to (a) in both.

1. Should the owner app flag a waiting support request outside Settings? This is the third part of the finding's suggested fix; it is not in the finding's Expected.
 (a) Not in this fix (recommended under the charter's exact-finding rule). The request can be reached at Settings › Support access, and support tells the owner out of band.
 (b) Client-side badge. owner-app/app/_layout.tsx:273-291 already badges Today from reporting.dashboard.owner. Add a `tenancy.support.list({ openOnly: true, limit: 20 })` read with staleTime 60 s, and badge the Settings rail item with the number of grants whose supportDecision is 'waiting'. No contract change; one extra owner-only read per app load.
 (c) Server-side count. Add `supportRequestsWaiting` to reporting.dashboard.owner. That is a contract change plus README regeneration, with reporting reading through tenancy's index export.

2. The kit's `<Segments>` silently drops options past three, in both renderers. Owner Settings 'Support access' is not the third screen it broke. Two manager surfaces are already repaired: inbound 'Purchase orders' and the credit-note reasons. Owner Settings is repaired by this fix. The owner app still drops four more today:
 - 'quote' (app/prices/index.tsx:233-246)
 - 'bounds' (app/staff/index.tsx:134-146)
 - 'brands' (app/stock/catalog.tsx:143-156)
 - 'This FY' (src/lib/ui.tsx:219-242 RangeSegments, on billing, credit notes, money, books and receipts)
No finding covers them.
 (a) File a new finding for those four owner surfaces, and keep the kit's silent slice (status quo: each screen picks Chips itself).
 (b) (a), plus a development-only console.warn in both renderers when items.length > 3, with a parity test.
 (c) (a), plus type items as a 2- or 3-element tuple so typecheck fails. This breaks the `.map()` call sites (admin interval, delivery reasons, owner POD policy) and every four-item literal above until each is fixed.

reviewNotes:
Adversarial review (read-only). Changes from the submitted plan:
1. Lapsed requests. The submitted time filter on hour options did hide a lapsed ask, but only implicitly. supportDecision now applies the console's own askLapsed() rule (admin-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:365-372), so the console's 'Lapsed' and the owner's missing card always agree. The spec names the lapsed case (dos_qa 7232298a).
2. Stale hour choice. Added chosenHours(): a picked value is sent only while it is still offered, and otherwise the hours asked are used. The submitted `hoursById[id] ?? initialHours` could send an hour whose window closed while the page stayed open.
3. Refusal. The submitted plan put useRefusal in as 'the last child of the body', which reads like a hook call inside JSX. The amended plan copies the manager app's `<Refusal>` and `stayOpen` (manager-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:194-234) into frontend/owner-app/src/lib/ui.tsx. That is the existing pattern, and it keeps the hook at a component's top level.
4. Tests.
- The source-reading spec moves to its own file, frontend/owner-app/src/settings-views.test.ts, as sales-app/src/order-entry-layout.test.ts does.
- The owner test script is `vitest run --dir src` (the sales-app form).
- The stub now also covers windowClosesAt (counts from Date.now()) and chosenHours (returns 4), so every spec is red on an assertion.
5. Honesty lines.
- Added 'Counted from when they asked' under the hour chips: 'Approve for 4 h' on a 4 h ask answered 3 h later opens only one hour.
- The history register's reason column is headed 'Why they are asking' instead of 'Note for the person who asked' (index.tsx:199). Reading the reason is part of the finding's Expected.
6. The Segments import stays: settings-pod (:378-383) still uses it.
7. Verify could not be run as written on a batch-2 template copy.
- That template carries a LIVE 72 h Tarsun window (approved at template build, expires 16 Sep), and the console hides 'Ask for support access' while a window is live (admin-app/src/lib/support.tsx:340, :504-510).
